Now I see it! At line 603-604:
```c
if (c == '%')
{
    if (!(g_ascii_isxdigit (p[0]) ||
          g_ascii_isxdigit (p[1])))
        goto error;
```

When `c == '%'` and `p` points to the last byte of the input (or past it), `p[0]` and `p[1]` read past the end of the buffer!

But wait, this is in `_g_uri_parse_authority` in `gnetworkaddress.c`, not in `guri.c`. The task says the vulnerability is in `guri.c`.

Let me re-read the task description: "A vulnerability exists in the URI scope parsing code in guri, where the parser can read past the end of a URI if it encounters an incorrect %-escaped character."

"URI scope parsing code in guri" - this is the zone ID (scope ID) parsing in `parse_host` in `guri.c`. The zone ID is also called "scope ID" in IPv6 addresses.
